cards.front: Anticoagulant of choice throughout pregnancy is LMWH; warfarin is teratogenic at [___] weeks; DOACs are contraindicated.
cards.context:
LMWH does not cross the placenta, so it is the anticoagulant of choice in pregnancy. After birth, LMWH or warfarin is compatible with breastfeeding.

Warfarin crosses the placenta and is most teratogenic at 6-12 weeks; later exposure risks fetal intracranial bleeding.

Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) lack pregnancy safety data and are contraindicated. Use indication- and weight-appropriate LMWH dosing under the relevant protocol.

cards.front: Safer Baby Bundle: settle to sleep on the side from 28 weeks, because going to sleep supine is linked to late stillbirth; lying supine compresses the [___].
cards.context:
Going to sleep supine from 28 weeks is associated with late stillbirth (pooled adjusted odds ratio 2.63); either side appears equally safe.

Supine at 35-38 weeks, MRI shows IVC flow falls by about 85% and cardiac output by about 16% despite azygos collaterals: a plausible mechanism, not proven cause.

cards.front: Neonatal resuscitation: chest compressions if HR remains <60 after 30 seconds of effective positive pressure ventilation; ratio is [___]:1 (compressions to breaths).
cards.context:
Chest compressions added when HR <60 despite 30 sec of effective PPV. 3:1 ratio (3 compressions to 1 ventilation, ~120 events/min) maximises ventilation in the respiratory-arrest p.

Technique: two-thumb encircling hands (thumbs over lower sternum, fingers around the back), depth ⅓ of AP chest diameter, smooth rhythm. Reassess HR q30 sec.

cards.front: Asymptomatic bacteriuria is treated in pregnancy because it can progress to [___].
cards.context:
Outside pregnancy, bacteria in the urine without symptoms is usually left alone. In pregnancy, dilated ureters and urinary stasis let the infection climb to the kidney.

So pregnant women are screened at the first visit and treated if it is found.

cards.front: In meconium aspiration, partial ball-valve airway obstruction causes [___].
cards.context:
Partial airway obstruction produces ball-valve gas trapping; complete obstruction causes atelectasis. Uneven inflation increases the risk of air leak and pneumothorax.

Meconium also inactivates surfactant and causes chemical pneumonitis. Hypoxaemia and raised pulmonary vascular resistance can lead to persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn.

cards.front: A newborn with a waiter's-tip arm posture and preserved palmar grasp has the classic pattern of [___].
cards.context:
Erb palsy classically affects C5–C6: the shoulder is adducted and internally rotated, with an extended elbow and preserved grasp. Associated phrenic nerve injury can impair diaphragmatic movement.

Klumpke palsy affects C8–T1, causing hand weakness, clawing and absent grasp. Associated sympathetic injury may produce Horner syndrome.

cards.front: The maternal red-cell antibody especially associated with suppression of fetal erythropoiesis is [___].
cards.context:
Anti-D, anti-c and anti-K can cause severe fetal anaemia. Kell antibodies suppress erythropoiesis as well as causing haemolysis, so low titres do not establish safety.

Refer to maternal–fetal medicine as soon as anti-K is detected. Assess fetal antigen risk; surveillance for fetal anaemia uses middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity.

cards.front: Bedside features split antepartum haemorrhage: a soft uterus with painless bleeding suggests a low-segment placenta; a hard/woody uterus with painful bleeding suggests [___]. Speculum + urgent USS go first; digital vaginal exam is deferred until imaging excludes a low-segment implantation.
cards.context:
The two major causes of antepartum haemorrhage have opposing bedside signatures: placenta praevia (painless, soft uterus, often recurrent) versus abruption (painful, tense/woody uterus, fetal distress).

Workup is speculum + urgent USS first — digital vaginal exam is catastrophic if praevia is present and undiagnosed.

cards.front: In cord prolapse, the immediate action is to digitally [___] the presenting part while preparing for emergency caesarean section.
cards.context:
The presenting part compresses the cord against the pelvis, cutting off fetal blood flow — minutes matter. Pushing it back up with a hand relieves that compression and buys time for delivery.

Keep the cord inside and handle it as little as possible: exposure to cold air and physical handling trigger vasospasm that worsens fetal hypoxia, and replacing the cord is never attempted.

cards.front: Erb's palsy is a [___]-C6 brachial plexus injury producing 'waiter's tip' — arm adducted, internally rotated, elbow extended, wrist flexed.
cards.context:
Erb's palsy = upper trunk (C5-C6) brachial plexus injury, classically from excessive lateral head traction during difficult delivery (often after shoulder dystocia).

Deficit map: C5-C6 supplies deltoid, biceps, brachialis, supinator, supraspinatus, infraspinatus — arm hangs adducted, internally rotated, elbow extended, forearm pronated, wrist flexed ('waiter's tip').

Klumpke's palsy (C8-T1) is the lower-trunk injury → 'claw hand' with absent grasp.

cards.front: Trial of labour after caesarean: baseline uterine rupture risk is approximately 0.5% in experienced centres; risk doubles with oxytocin augmentation. Overall TOLAC success rate is around [___]%.
cards.context:
VBAC carries a small but real risk of uterine rupture along the previous scar — ~1:200 (0.5%) in experienced centres for a single previous transverse lower segment CS.

Risk doubles with oxytocin augmentation (over-stimulation stresses scar), rises with prior classical (vertical) incision (~5-10% — generally contraindicates VBAC), multiple previous CS.

VBAC success rate ~70%, lower without prior vaginal birth + recurrent CS indication.

cards.front: Neonatal resuscitation: start positive pressure ventilation (PPV) if HR <[___] or no spontaneous breathing; ventilation is the priority because most neonatal arrests are respiratory in origin.
cards.context:
Neonatal resus algorithm: first 30 sec — dry, stimulate, keep warm, position airway. 30-sec reassessment: if breathing inadequately OR HR <100.

After 30 sec PPV: HR rising + breathing improving → continue support and wean; HR remains <100 → optimise ventilation (MR SOPA); HR <60 despite effective ventilation → add chest compressions 3:1 with breaths.

cards.front: The standard pre-ductal pulse oximetry site in a newborn is the [___].
cards.context:
The right hand samples pre-ductal blood; a foot samples post-ductal blood. A lower foot saturation can reflect right-to-left ductal shunting in persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn.

Paired readings also support critical congenital heart disease screening. A gradient is not diagnostic of PPHN, and a normal screen does not exclude every cardiac lesion.

cards.front: During newborn resuscitation, start chest compressions if HR remains below 60/min despite [___] of effective positive-pressure ventilation.
cards.context:
Neonatal resuscitation escalates in 30-sec reassessment intervals. First 30 s: dry, stimulate, keep warm, position airway, assess.

Start PPV for inadequate breathing or HR <100/min. If HR remains <60/min after 30 seconds of effective ventilation, add compressions at a 3:1 compression-to-ventilation ratio.

Most neonatal arrests are respiratory in origin — EFFECTIVE ventilation is highest-yield; if HR doesn't respond to PPV, optimise ventilation FIRST (MR SOPA) before assuming cardiac.

cards.front: A significant magnetic resonance feature of adenomyosis is junctional zone thickening greater than [___].
cards.context:
The junctional zone is the inner muscle beneath the endometrium. Adenomyosis thickens it, which is one reason MRI is used when ultrasound cannot separate this from a fibroid.

The same scan can show very small foci and can tell an adenomyoma from a fibroid when several large fibroids are present.

cards.front: In Australia, miscarriage means pregnancy loss before [___]; the most common cause of early miscarriage is fetal aneuploidy.
cards.context:
Pooled international data estimate miscarriage in about 15% of recognised pregnancies; this is not an Australian registry estimate. Chromosomal abnormalities cause many early miscarriages.

Further assessment depends on timing, recurrence and clinical findings. Birth-registration rules are separate from this clinical definition.
